summary: John Avery was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Amherst College, the University of Tübingen, the Humboldt University of Berlin, and under William Dwight Whitney. He held posts as Professor of Greek at Grinnell College (1870–1877) and Bowdoin College (1877).

John Borthwick Gilchrist worked in linguistics and Indology, having studied at the Royal High School, George Heriot's School, and the University of Edinburgh. He served with the East India Company (~1782–1804), Fort William College (~1800–1804), and East India Company College (1806).
John Brockington is an Indologist whose career included serving as Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Edinburgh (attested 1987 and 2003).

John Brough was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. Educated at Edinburgh and Cambridge under Arthur Berriedale Keith and Harold Walter Bailey, his career included posts at the British Museum, SOAS, the University of London, and Cambridge (1967–1984).
John Buescher is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who completed his doctoral dissertation at the University of Virginia in 1982 and served as Director at Voice of America (attested 2001).
John C. Huntington was a scholar in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and history and archaeology. He served as a professor at Ohio State University (attested 1987–1990 and 2000).

John C. Maraldo worked in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. His career includes posts at the University of North Florida (attested 1988), where he was later distinguished professor emeritus of philosophy (attested 2015).
John Chadwick was a linguist and archaeologist who studied at St Paul's School and Corpus Christi College, Cambridge (~1939–1946). He later held a post at the University of Cambridge (~1952–1984).
John Claude White was active in Tibetology and history/archaeology. He was educated at Rugby School (~1867–1872) and the Royal Indian Engineering College (~1873–1876).

John Clifford Holt is a religious and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Gustavus Adolphus College, Graduate Theological Union, and the University of Chicago under Stanley Jeyaraja Tambiah. He held posts at Bowdoin College (~1978–2020) and the University of Calgary (2006).
John Collinson Nesfield was a scholar in linguistics and Indology who completed his education at Highgate School and Merton College (~1856–1860).

John Corrigan is a scholar of religious studies and history/archaeology who studied at the University of Chicago (~1976–1982). He held posts at Harvard University, the University of Virginia, Arizona State University, and Florida State University (~2001).

John Crook, a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, studied at Sherborne School, Southampton, Jesus College, and under Sheng Yen. He founded the Western Chan Fellowship (1997) and held posts at the University of Bristol and Université Bouddhique Européenne.

John D. Dunne is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. Educated at Amherst, CIHTS, Harvard Divinity School, and Harvard University under Nagatomi, Eckel, Hallisey, and Tripathi, he held posts at CIHTS, Harvard, Antioch, Wisconsin-Madison, and Emory.
John Daido Loori was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under and succeeded Taizan Maezumi. He served as Abbot of Zen Mountain Monastery from approximately 1980 to 2009.
John Daishin Buksbazen is a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied at the Zen Center of Los Angeles under Taizan Maezumi and Bernie Glassman (attested 2002).
John Dowson was a scholar of Indology and linguistics who held academic posts at University College London and at the Staff College, Camberley, where he was Professor of Hindustani (~1855–1877).

John E. Cort is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison and Harvard University (~1982–1989). He held a post as professor at Denison University (~1993).

John Faithfull Fleet was an Indologist and historian/archaeologist educated at University College London (~1865–1867). He served in the Bombay Civil Service and Indian Civil Service (~1867–1897) and as Epigraphist for the Government of India (1883–1886).

John Gombojab Hangin was a linguist and Central Asian specialist who studied at Hokkaido, Columbia, and Indiana University. He held posts at Johns Hopkins, Georgetown, UC Berkeley, Columbia, and Indiana University (1964–1989).
